Title: Climate Research
Description: Study urban heat islands and identify the main sources of carbon emissions. This research will establish the scientific foundation of the project.

Title: User Surveys
Description: Interview residents and city planners to understand their environmental concerns. Focus on the data and features they need most.

Title: Data Analysis
Description: Collect existing temperature and pollution datasets from public sources. Analyze urban patterns to identify priority monitoring areas.

Title: Competitor Study
Description: Analyze existing climate monitoring platforms and environmental applications. Identify gaps that Urban Heat & Carbon Tracker can address.

Title: Sensor Prototype
Description: Build a basic sensor system to measure urban temperature and air quality. Test its accuracy in different outdoor environments.

Title: Dashboard Design
Description: Create an interactive dashboard displaying heat levels and carbon emissions. Prioritize clear visualizations and accessible information.

Title: Data Integration
Description: Connect public weather APIs and environmental databases. Establish a reliable system for collecting real-time data.

Title: Field Testing
Description: Deploy prototype sensors in selected urban locations. Evaluate their performance under real environmental conditions.

Title: Technical Hiring
Description: Recruit developers with experience in environmental data and web technologies. Prioritize technical expertise and commitment to climate action.

Title: Climate Experts
Description: Bring environmental scientists and urban planners into the team. Their knowledge will improve the accuracy and relevance of the platform.

Title: Marketing Team
Description: Recruit specialists to manage communication and community engagement. Build a team capable of promoting environmental awareness.

Title: Community Partners
Description: Partner with local environmental organizations and volunteers. Their participation will strengthen data collection and public trust.

Title: Core Dashboard
Description: Develop an MVP featuring live urban temperature monitoring and carbon emission estimates. Keep the interface simple and functional.

Title: Heat Alerts
Description: Introduce basic notifications for dangerous urban temperature levels. Help residents identify potential heat-related risks.

Title: Emission Reports
Description: Add automated reports showing estimated carbon emissions by location. Provide users with understandable environmental insights.

Title: Public Map
Description: Launch an interactive map showing urban heat zones and pollution hotspots. Allow users to explore environmental conditions across the city.

Title: Market Survey
Description: Test the concept with potential users and local authorities. Measure demand for accessible urban climate data.

Title: Stakeholder Interviews
Description: Present the MVP to municipal representatives and environmental organizations. Gather feedback on practical applications and partnership opportunities.

Title: Pricing Strategy
Description: Explore sustainable funding models including municipal subscriptions and grants. Ensure the platform can remain accessible to the public.

Title: Impact Assessment
Description: Estimate the potential environmental and social impact of the platform. Use measurable indicators to evaluate its contribution to SDG 13.

Title: Platform Expansion
Description: Expand the platform with advanced data processing and additional environmental indicators. Improve its ability to analyze large urban datasets.

Title: AI Predictions
Description: Integrate machine learning to forecast urban heat patterns. Help city planners identify future climate risks.

Title: Mobile Integration
Description: Develop a mobile-friendly version with location-based environmental insights. Make climate information accessible to residents on the move.

Title: Security Upgrade
Description: Strengthen data protection and system reliability. Implement secure storage and regular backups.

Title: Open Data Access
Description: Publish selected environmental datasets through an open API. Encourage researchers and developers to build complementary climate solutions.

Title: City Partnerships
Description: Establish partnerships with municipal governments and urban planning departments. Integrate the platform into local climate strategies.

Title: Sensor Network
Description: Expand sensor deployment across multiple neighborhoods. Improve the geographical coverage and accuracy of environmental monitoring.

Title: Analytics Upgrade
Description: Introduce advanced analytics for tracking long-term temperature and emission trends. Provide actionable insights for decision-makers.

Title: DPG Documentation
Description: Prepare technical documentation and transparent project governance policies. Clearly explain the platform's architecture and public value.

Title: Open Source
Description: Publish the source code under an appropriate open-source license. Encourage developers to inspect and improve the platform.

Title: Privacy Review
Description: Conduct a comprehensive privacy and security assessment. Ensure responsible handling of location and user data.

Title: DPG Assessment
Description: Evaluate the project against Digital Public Good standards. Identify improvements needed for transparency and responsible technology.

Title: Public Launch
Description: Release Urban Heat & Carbon Tracker to the public. Promote its features through environmental campaigns and community networks.

Title: Launch Campaign
Description: Organize a citywide awareness campaign to introduce the platform. Encourage residents to explore local climate conditions.

Title: Government Rollout
Description: Present the platform to government agencies and municipal partners. Demonstrate how environmental insights can support climate policies.

Title: Global Outreach
Description: Share the project with international climate organizations and development communities. Explore opportunities for replication in other cities.
